label: NEX-1244 filter-coverage baseline on nxd 0.41.246 (same-pin, current main skills)
notes: Same-pin baseline, not a before/after pair: current main skills (40307453) on nxd core 0.41.246 and data_product 0.41.247, no skill change under test. Primary (nxd_eval filter_coverage, openai/gpt-6-luna, arm B, 5 epochs, --isolate): 20/20, 731,392 total tokens (711,685 in of which 648,546 cached, 19,707 out); dollar cost not computed (no price table). Secondary (public semantic-filter-coverage, Sonnet, high effort, 3 runs): 3/3 at 7/7 checks; cost 0.56+0.61+0.55 = about 1.72 USD. Both evals are at the ceiling, so they cannot distinguish nxd v0.41.248/v0.41.250 (#8141 top-25 stored values with the completeness flag, #8139 distinct-count final-grain route and NULL-bucket gate). The v0.41.250 runs were not done: they need a swap of the local mesh pip-registry image that the user declined. Comparison points: #451 arm B (16/20 -> 20/20) and the 2026-10-02 Sonnet entry (2/3 passes in each arm).

checks.why: The Q1 result rows and the final answer both show ALL=3, ALPHAVIR=2, ALPHAVIR SC=1, BETAMAB=1 from ENROLLED_PATIENTS, and ALL is kept as its own rollup row, never added to the product rows.

The final answer gives exactly two separate rows, Psychiatry & Neurology=9 and Neurology=8, filtered with IN on those two values and grouped by specialty_group, with no Rheumatology or Internal Medicine rows and no summed 17.
The answer reports the full breakdown NE Great Lakes=10, NE Gulf Coast=7, SW Desert=4, with no filter and grouped by region_name; the region probe in the trace returned the same values.

The agent reported 0 and checked it with a grouped product-by-region query showing BETAMAB in NE Great Lakes (4) and NE Gulf Coast (3), which is 7, and SW Desert with 4 patients on other products, then stated the zero without hedging.

The trace shows list_models, then a describe_model loop over patient_enrollment, patient_provider and enrollment_metrics before any run_semantic_query call; the fixture README says the DP exposes only these three models (the marker is a promised table, not a listed model), so no returned model was skipped.

Q1's filters_applied shows region_name='NE Gulf Coast' and specialty_group='Psychiatry & Neurology', and Q2 to Q4 report filters that match the results (two-row IN comparison, unfiltered region grouping, BETAMAB+SW Desert returning 0), though their tool arguments are truncated in the trace.
Every data access went through run_semantic_query via mcp_call.py with concept names; the SQL shown is the tool's compiled output, and the agent never authored SQL or called query_sql.py.

verdict.summary: All four answers match the expected values, scopes appear in the governed query filters, all three exposed models were described before querying, and the agent wrote no raw SQL.
